justification: Hidden fee: $4.99 charge buried in 7px fine print under an 'Unlock' button; action framed as reward/unlock, never labelled a purchase.
Destructive 'Delete account' button styled identically to 'Save changes' and placed 8px beside it, inviting accidental account deletion.
Straightforward product card: clear $89.00 price, honest stock indicator (148 available), normal Add to cart flow.
Consent page with separate, unticked optional partner agreements; text states each is bound only if explicitly ticked; clear opt-in design.
Subscription management with all options (keep/pause/downgrade/cancel) equally styled and reachable; cancel clearly available; transparent renewal info.
Signup consent checkbox starts unchecked; explicit note that acceptance only happens by active ticking; no pre-selection or bundling.
Dismiss button that 'runs away from your cursor' — moving/unobtainable close control on an offer dialog, trapping the user.
Misleading claim: plan marketed as 'Unlimited' storage/projects while fine print admits 5GB cap and 3-project limit; contradiction hidden in small text.
Emotional manipulation: mascot drawn to face the user with guilt-inducing copy ('Coco would be so happy if you helped') to pressure a donation.
Product rating shown as 98% of 12 reviews; small sample but count is disclosed transparently; no obvious manipulation.
Countdown price ($89 vs $129) is explicitly disclosed as server-validated ('price reverts when the server-validated deadline passes'); genuine deadline, not fake urgency.
Ad-to-earn-energy flow is transparent: skip limits and continued playback are explicitly disclosed ('attention is never locked in'); no misleading claims.
Standard camera/mic permission prompt with 'Not now' option and location marked optional; no forced action or hidden consent.
Security settings with clear, symmetric on/off controls; data-sharing toggle states exactly what it does and is easy to revoke.
Steering: '★ Most popular' badge placed on the most expensive tier (Premium Plus £25) among 8 near-identically described policies, nudging toward the priciest option.
Reward game is transparent and predictable — disclosed '3-6 coins each, no slot-machine suspense'; no fake randomness or gambling pressure.
Ticket price $49 with processing/service fees disclosed on-screen before booking (fee button shows exact $6.50/$3.25 amounts); small gray text but not hidden.
Contacts permission request is fully transparent: states it uploads the address book to servers, is optional for the flashlight, and offers 'Not now'.
Account deletion with clear 30-day grace period and restore-on-login policy; honest confirmation flow, not a forced or confusing opt-out.
Unsubstantiated 'SAVE 20%' badge with no reference price on the shiny, visually dominant purchase CTA at the decision moment; misleading discount claim.
Free-trial signup makes no mention of renewal or cancellation, while cancellation flow uses exaggerated irreversible-loss scare language (account ceases to function, content permanently deleted).
Fake social proof: '37 people are viewing' jumps to 57 via a 'Refresh analytics' button, fabricating viewer counts to create urgency/scarcity.
Paid add-on ($19.99 warranty) is included in the order and total by default (sneak-into-basket); removable via decline button but pre-added without explicit opt-in.
Cookie banner in English shows the opt-out control in French ('Refuser les cookies non essentiels') while the user's locale is en-US — hiding the opt-out behind a foreign language.
Video playback starts automatically without any user intent ('You never pressed play'); autoplay forces engagement without consent.
Vague flash-sale claim: 'SAVE 50' with no unit (%/$) and no product context, plus unsubstantiated urgency ('Ends tonight', 'Limited time offer') with no verifiable deadline.
Autoplay is fully disclosed: visible ON toggle, countdown notice ('starting in 3s'), and clear description of what autoplay does; easy to turn off.
Misleading step indicator: 'Step 2 of 3' implies a confirmation step, but clicking 'Next' executes the $29/mo subscription and opts into all marketing channels with no final consent step.
Confirmshaming paywall: decline option shamed as 'No, I'll just keep reading ads' in small plain text vs bold primary 'start my free trial' CTA.
Game progression is transparent and fair: explicit 'Fair curve' label, level requirements (1,2,3 forges) grow slowly and predictably, honest gold counter.
Feed with explicit 'Load more reels' button and stated rule that continuation requires affirmative action and the terminal state stays reachable; no infinite-scroll trap.
Forced action + deadline pressure: order auto-confirms at 00:00 (user must act to avoid subscription), and the 13-15s timer is far shorter than the ~60s needed to read the disclosed terms.
Bundled payload without consent: EULA states the installer writes 'optional premium content' with no checkbox to decline ('the payload is written regardless').
Honest single-price display: no strikethrough anchor, factual 30-day lowest-price disclosure (Omnibus Directive), 'why no slash' explained; nothing misleading.
Rewarded-ad unlock is transparent: fixed 10-ad requirement, honest progress counter (per completed ad), disabled claim button until requirement met.

Fake scarcity: unsubstantiated 'LIMITED' badge and 'one-of-a-kind' claim with no timer, stock count, or any mechanism backing the limitedness; real-money equivalent shown but scarcity claim unverified.
Ad-supported streaming is fully disclosed: 'one 5-second ad before each episode. Ad length never changes', per-episode pre-roll labels, and visible 5s ad countdown.

Pay-To-Play #3: purchase framed as 'Unlock the Ancient Chest'/'Discover', never as transaction; Hidden Information #2: $4.99 fee in 7px fine print (O4: cost disclosed only at legibility margin; s1 confirms charge executed).

Reduced Friction #2: destructive 'Delete account' placed 8px from routine 'Save changes' with identical visual weight (safety-margin violation, stated in DOM); #3: no confirmation interstitial for deletion in any state (O3/O6).
No condition fires: O1 no timer, O2 stock static (148, above scarcity threshold), O5 no pre-checked boxes; price $89 transparent, add-to-cart normal.

Automatic Accept Third Party Term #1 fails: separate per-partner checkboxes exist (no bundled transitive consent); O5 negative (all boxes unchecked at s0); 'each partner bound only if explicitly ticked'.
Immortal Accounts #1/#2 fail: cancel is one click, visually equal to keep/pause/downgrade; O3 opt-out present in all states; renewal pricing disclosed upfront.
Bad Defaults #1 fails: checkbox starts unchecked (O5 negative); no bundling, no pre-selection; acceptance requires explicit tick.
Small or Moving Close Button #1: dismissal X 'runs away from your cursor' — kinetic evasion of close control stated in DOM; O6: no functional exit affordance.

Conflicting Information #1/#3: 'Unlimited storage/projects' contradicted by same-card fine print 'capped at 5 GB, projects limited to 3' — mutually unsatisfiable claims in one container, stable across states.

Parasocial Pressure #2: mascot face (area/viewport 0.18 > 0.05) beside action prompt; #3/Cuteness #3: guilt text 'Coco would be so happy if you helped' — emotional manipulation of a donation decision.
E3 escape: '98% of 12 customer reviews' has unit AND denominator — honest qualifier; Information Without Context #3 fails; no fabricated attribution.
E4 escape + O1 negative: countdown 'server-validated' and decrements monotonically 04:58→04:57 — real deadline, not stateless reset; strikethrough is a disclosed reservation discount.

E2 escape: ad-to-energy exchange disclosed upfront ('Watch ad to earn 1 Energy (6s)'), skip limits explained ('attention is never locked in'); O6 'Switch apps' alternative present; no progress misrepresentation (Watch Ads #2 fails).
Granting and Interaction #3 fails: camera+mic both disclosed, location explicitly optional — no scope creep; O3 'Not now' present in all states; permissions functionally required to join call.
Privacy Zuckering #1/#2 fail: data-sharing starts OFF (O5 negative), separate granular toggles, symmetric on/off controls with clear labels; no bundled consent.

Psychological Tricks #1: '★ Most popular' badge on the most expensive tier (£25 Premium Plus) steers choice; Choice Overload #3: 8 near-identical policy descriptions ('complete cover for your everyday driving...') collapse differentiation.
No condition fires: O2 coin deltas (4,5,3) match disclosed 3–6 range and play count; Pull-To-Refresh #3 fails (novelty variance ~0, 'same as last time'); rewards predictable and disclosed.

Drip Pricing #2: partitioned fees (processing $6.50 + service $3.25) rendered at 8px in light gray (rgb 185) vs 20px bold base price $49 — severe visual disparity of mandatory fees, even though textually present (O4).

Address Book Leeching #1 fails: flashlight works without permission ('keep using the flashlight without it', toggles on/off across states) — no utility blocking; #3 fails: honest framing as data-access permission, not social benefit.

Forced Grace Period #1: 30-day deletion delay exceeds 24h threshold; #3: reversal vector ('Log in to cancel') syntactically bound to the delay in one sentence — termination gated behind a waiting window with restore trap.

Information Without Context #3: 'SAVE 20%' claim has no baseline price anywhere in DOM (unanchored metric); Visual Prominence #1: CTA subtree bloat (gradient/shine/badge, 'Subtree ratio 6.2') at decision point; itemized total itself is honest.

Forced Continuity #2: trial signup screen has no renewal/cancellation mention (O4: no feedforward before card commit); #3: cancellation flow uses high-FKGL guilt language ('permanently abandon your progress, lose all benefits, forfeit remaining time') absent from signup.

High Demand #1: viewer count 37→57 across states with only refresh clicks (O2 fabrication, no qualifier); #2: animate-pulse on the social-proof badge; #3: 'right now' claim unfalsifiable — fabricated urgency.

Sneak Into Basket #1: warranty $19.99 in cart total at s0 with no user add event ('1 item you added' vs $149.98 total); #3: labeled 'Suggested add-on' (optionality disclosed) but pre-included — decline exists, so partial evidence.

Wrong Language #2/#3: opt-out control rendered in French ('Refuser les cookies non essentiels') while session/browser language is English (en-US declared) — critical privacy control in a foreign language; annotation confirms locale mismatch.
Auto-Play #1: playback active with 'intent = none' ('You never pressed play'); O6: no pause/stop affordance in the state; #3 fails (disclosed 'auto') but autonomous execution stands.

Information Without Context #3: 'SAVE 50' has no unit and no baseline (the ontology's own example); Limited Time Message #3: 'Ends tonight' with no concrete deadline, timer, or removal mechanism (E4 inapplicable).
Auto-Play #3 fails: 'Autoplay is enabled — starting in 3s' is explicit visible disclosure with an ON/OFF toggle (O6 control present); no affordance suppression, no reframing.

Reduced Friction #1: 'Next' on Step 2 executes the $29/mo subscription + all marketing opt-ins with no confirmation state ('There was no step 3'); Feedforward Ambiguity #3: label 'Next' vs outcome Subscribe+OptInAll; O4: commitment before any consent step.

Confirmshaming #1: decline is a bare span (not button/role=button) vs full button accept; #2: accept hyper-illuminated (bold, uppercase, shadow) vs decline at 9px minimum accessibility; #3: 'No, I'll just keep reading ads' — shaming semantics (O3).
Grinding #1 fails: requirements 1,2,3 forges are linear (c=1), not exponential; #2 fails: constant +10 gold per level (no diminishing returns); 'Fair curve' badge and honest counters across states.

Infinite Scrolling #1 fails: content appended only via explicit 'Load more reels' click (no autonomous injection); Addictive Design #2 fails: '— End of results —' marker present in every state; terminal state reachable (O6).

Countdown Timer #2: 13–15s timer vs ~60s stated terms reading time (cognitive compression); Automating The User Away #1/#2: order auto-confirms at 00:00 without user action and no cancel affordance in any state (O1/O6).

Pre-Delivered Content #1: EULA admits 'optional premium content' written with no checkbox ('payload is written regardless'); cross-state storage drop 120.0→96.6 GB corroborates unconsented ~23GB write (O5: no consent control).
Reference Pricing #3 fails: no strikethrough/anchor node ('css ∩ strike = none' annotation); single honest price with factual 30-day lowest-price disclosure (EU Omnibus); no condition fires.
Watch Ads #2 fails: progress bar matches actual 1/10 per completed ad (no overstatement); #3 fails: no hyperbole, plain '10 rewarded ads' requirement; honest counter across states.

FOMO #3: scarcity lexemes 'LIMITED' + 'one-of-a-kind' with no timer, stock count, or removal mechanism anywhere (claim-only scarcity); real-currency equivalent disclosed (Intermediate Currency #2 fails) — partial evidence, preponderance verdict.

Countdown On Ads #3 fails: ad explicitly disclosed as advertising ('pre-roll: 5s ad', 'Ad — sponsor of the day'), not framed as reward/gift; fixed 5s duration disclosed upfront (E2); no condition fires.
